definition: General Language Understanding Evaluation, a collection of diverse natural language understanding tasks used to benchmark NLP models.
details: GLUE was influential in driving progress on pretrained language models in the years before large generative LLMs became dominant, and was later followed by the harder SuperGLUE benchmark as models began to saturate it.

explainer.lead: GLUE is a shared set of language-understanding tests for comparing NLP models. It helped researchers measure progress in pretrained language models, until strong results began to saturate the benchmark and prompted the harder SuperGLUE.

tiers.eli5: GLUE is like a decathlon for computer programs that read language: instead of testing just one skill, it gives them several different challenges. A program that does well across the challenges is considered better at understanding language. Eventually, the best programs found the tests too easy, so a harder follow-up called SuperGLUE was introduced.
tiers.practitioner: Use GLUE to compare pretrained language models across a common collection of natural-language-understanding tasks rather than relying on a single task. Report task results consistently when comparing models, and remember that saturation can make differences among strong systems less informative; SuperGLUE was introduced as a harder successor.
tiers.paperLevel: GLUE, or General Language Understanding Evaluation, defines multi-task benchmark evaluation over a diverse collection of natural-language-understanding tasks. It was influential in assessing progress on pretrained language models before large generative LLMs became dominant. Its principal historical limitation was saturation as model performance improved, leading to SuperGLUE.

explainer.example: For illustration, suppose a model’s result rises from 70 to 80 on one task and from 75 to 85 on another after additional pretraining. These hypothetical numbers show how task results can be compared across model versions; they are not reported GLUE scores or an official aggregation rule.

explainer.measures: GLUE measures how well NLP models handle a diverse collection of natural-language-understanding tasks. Using multiple tasks gives a broader comparison than evaluating a model on only one language problem.
howScored: Evaluate the model on each task in the collection.
Compare its task results with those of other models.
Use the results as a broad language-understanding benchmark.
explainer.typicalResults: Model results improved substantially as GLUE helped drive work on pretrained language models. Eventually, models began to saturate the benchmark, making a harder successor useful.
caveats: Saturation reduces its ability to distinguish strong models.
It evaluates language understanding, not the full range of generative LLM behavior.
